ds: Victims are deceived or coerced into authorising a payment to an account controlled by a criminal, often under a false pretext such as a safe-account request, a fake invoice or an invented purchase. Because the customer authorises the payment, controls rely on spotting behavioural change and mule receiving accounts.

cn.rt: Customer-authorised payments from everyday/savings accounts, often under phone coaching; branch tellers can intervene.

rat: Customer-authorised push payments in digital channels with live-call and remote-access signals.

ind.n: Payment to new payee under apparent time pressure
ind.cx: Victim-side: a first payment of unusually high value to a newly created payee, made quickly after a phone call or message and often outside normal patterns.
ind.fp: Genuine house purchases, one-off large bills or planned gifts to new payees.
ind.ds: Victim-side: a first payment of unusually high value to a newly created payee, made quickly after a phone call or message and often outside normal patterns.

ind.n: Customer on an active call while paying
ind.cx: Victim-side: session signals show the customer is on a live phone call, navigating hesitantly, or following dictation during online banking.
ind.fp: Customers legitimately on hand-free calls with family or advisers.
ind.ds: Customer is on an active phone call, hesitant or following dictated instructions while depositing cash or making an online payment.
ind.cn: Customer on a live call while transacting

ind.n: Evasive or scripted answers about payment purpose
ind.cx: Victim-side: when asked about the payment, the customer gives rehearsed, inconsistent or irritated answers, or says they were told to mislead the bank.
ind.fp: Privacy-minded customers or those unsure of terminology.
ind.ds: When asked about a transaction, the customer gives vague, rehearsed, inconsistent or shifting explanations of its purpose, source or counterparties.
ind.cn: Unable or unwilling to explain transaction purpose or origin

ind.n: Remote-access software present during banking session
ind.cx: Victim-side: remote desktop or screen-sharing tools detected while the customer logs in or pays.
ind.fp: IT support or family helping a customer with consent.
ind.ds: Remote-desktop, screen-sharing, emulator or scripted-control tools are detected during onboarding, login or payment sessions.
ind.cn: Remote-access, emulator or automation tools in session

ind.n: Sudden liquidation of savings or investments to fund payments
ind.cx: Victim-side: movement of long-held savings, fixed deposits or investments into the current account followed by outbound transfers.
ind.fp: Home deposits, life events or planned purchases.
ind.ds: Savings, investments or assets are sold abruptly, followed by withdrawal or transfer.
ind.cn: Sudden liquidation of savings or assets

ind.n: Beneficiary account name mismatch or no-match result
ind.cx: Victim-side: confirmation-of-payee check returns no match or close match and the customer proceeds regardless.
ind.fp: Typos, trading names or joint accounts producing benign mismatches.
ind.ds: Victim-side: confirmation-of-payee check returns no match or close match and the customer proceeds regardless.

ind.n: Receiving account rapidly forwards incoming credits
ind.cx: Mule-side: funds credited by multiple unrelated individuals are moved out within minutes or hours to other accounts, cash or crypto.
ind.fp: Pass-through for legitimate marketplace sellers or agents.
ind.ds: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.

ind.n: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
ind.cx: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.
ind.fp: Fundraising, club accounts or small traders with genuine many-to-one inflows.
ind.ds: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.

ind.n: Payment narrative or reference suggests safe-account or investment script
ind.cx: Victim-side: references such as 'safe account', 'HMRC', 'fees' or crypto platform names appear alongside atypical transfers.
ind.fp: Genuine references to tax or investment platforms.
ind.ds: Payment narratives or references contain wording linked to scams such as safe accounts or investment schemes.

ind.n: Multiple prior scam alerts or repeat victimisation
ind.cx: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.
ind.fp: Customers who have since become aware and are genuinely transacting.
ind.ds: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.

Checks the payee name against the destination account before release and warns on no-match or close-match, and flags payee-name mismatches against contracted entities. It interrupts misdirected, spoofed and fraudulent payments.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.
